description: Bridgey Protocol v1 freeze baseline (docs/protocol-v1.md): every v1 core, extension and deprecated entry of protocol/messages.json and a hash of each vector case that pins one, as recorded by protocol/tools/v1_freeze.py --write-baseline. Proposal: report only while frozen is false.

transport.framing: UTF-8 JSON object per line, terminated by LF; a CR before LF is ignored
transport.onMalformedFrame: close the session before dispatch (oversized frame, invalid UTF-8, not a JSON object, missing or wrong-typed envelope field)
transport.onUnknownKind: ignore the message and keep the session
transport.replayWindow: per session, the last 256 accepted messageId values, oldest evicted first

binaryFrames.when: only on a protocol 2 session (envelope tags on): read once the session is authenticated; sent only to a peer whose latest features.update shows files_fast_draft1 true
binaryFrames.header: 1 byte marker 0xB1, 1 byte kind, 4 bytes body length (big-endian, 1 to 1048677); the marker cannot start a JSON frame or UTF-8 text
binaryFrames.body: 1 byte ID length L (1 to 64), L bytes ID (printable ASCII: the transfer ID, or the speed test ID), 8 bytes sequence (big-endian, 0 to 2^53-1), 12 bytes AES-GCM nonce, ciphertext and 16-byte tag; plaintext 1 to 1048576 bytes. The AES-GCM key is HMAC-SHA-256(session key, bridgey-fast-frame-key-v2)
binaryFrames.associatedData: length-prefixed like the protocol 2 envelope tag input: bridgey-fast-frame-v2, the sending device's ID, the kind (decimal), the ID, the sequence (decimal). The AES-GCM tag stands in for the envelope tag

kinds.1: files.chunk: the same chunk as the JSON files.chunk, up to 1 MiB; the receiver acknowledges each with files.chunk.ack
kinds.2: speed.data: speed test bytes, acknowledged with speed.ack and dropped

binaryFrames.onUnknownKind: once its tag verifies (the kind is in the associated data), skip the frame and keep the session; a failed tag is dropped and counted
binaryFrames.onBadLength: close the session (the stream can no longer be split)
binaryFrames.onMalformedOrUndecryptable: drop and count with the frames dropped for a bad envelope tag; 16 close the connection
binaryFrames.replay: not in the messageId window: per kind and ID the sequence must rise (the 256 most recently used IDs are remembered); file chunks must also follow on without gaps

sessionId.note: empty only in pairing.cancel sent before the session ID is known

messageId.note: UUID; required by every encrypted message that uses the replay window. An empty optional string counts as absent

sequence.note: an integral JSON number; each kind checks its own range

commitment.note: protocol 2: base64 SHA-256 commitment to the first-pairing offer's ephemeral key, opened by pairing.reveal

protocolVersion.note: in pairing.offer and pairing.answer: the highest protocol the sender speaks; absent means 1

reason.note: in pairing.cancel: mismatch, cancelled, timeout, busy, rate_limited, not_armed, needs_protocol_2 or not_trusted; older peers send none

tag.note: protocol 2: base64 HMAC-SHA-256 over the sender's device ID and every other envelope field, on every frame after pairing when both ends sent protocolVersion 2

shape.note: Codes from email (docs/codes-from-email.md): the phone sets it while notifications and its Also read codes in email switch are on for that Mac; the Mac while notifications for that phone, Codes from messages and Also read codes in email are on. Needs sms_codes_draft1 too. Gates the emailApp and preview fields of notifications.post, and redacted on mail notifications
the device serves browsing (places.files, media.*, places.download) and accepts uploads; Macs advertise it false
the device accepts folders.offer from its peer; phones check it before sending a folder to a Mac

the Mac sets it when Mac actions is on and granted to that phone (off by default), the phone when its Mac actions switch is on for that Mac; gates actions.*. Both apps keep it as a switch, but a non-boolean value reads false like every draft key
the Mac understands quick.request links action open (Open on Mac); set while Web links is on for that phone. Phones advertise nothing
the device understands focus.state; advertised while either Focus direction (share, follow) is on
the phone takes photos for that Mac (its switch, on by default); the Mac sets it while Files is on for that phone; gates camera.*. The photo comes back over files.v1 with cameraRequestId

the device sends updates.status and understands updates.start (Update all); edition builds that have the feature always advertise it, and the status field remoteStart says whether this device lets others start its update; the optional status fields auto and busy and the start field auto (Update all devices automatically) are ignored by builds without them

fast transfers: the device reads binary frames (transport.binaryFrames) and paces chunks on a byte window. Both apps always advertise it when they support it (a capability, not a setting). Between two peers that show it, every files.chunk is a binary frame of up to 1 MiB (senders use 256 KiB), every chunk is acknowledged with files.chunk.ack, and senders keep their unacknowledged bytes within a delay-based window of 512 KiB to 32 MiB. Gates speed.*

Text messages: SMS conversations on the Mac. The phone sets it while its Text messages switch is on for that Mac, the Mac while its Text messages setting is on; both off by default. Gates sms.* and the smsReply and smsThreadId fields of notifications.post
the device syncs settings and feature switches with that peer: its global switch (on by default) and its switch for that peer are both on; gates settings.*

Connect anywhere (docs/connect-anywhere.md): the device runs the edition's QUIC tunnel and routes and understands connect.*; advertised to every peer while Connect away from home is on and the core library loaded. Tunnel sessions sign bridgey-auth-v2 (protocol.md)

Agent devices (docs/protocol.md, agent devices): the agent sets it always; the phone sets it for each agent device. Gates agent.*. An agent's map lists what it can do; the phone's map to an agent lists what Rahul granted, and the phone never pushes its own clipboard, notifications, files, texts or settings to an agent
Agent grant Send you notifications: the phone sets it for an agent while the grant is on (its window not over); gates notify.post
Agent grant Ask you questions: the phone sets it for an agent while the grant is on; gates ask.*
Agent grant Ask for your clipboard: the phone sets it for an agent while the grant is on; gates clipboard.request (every request needs a tap)
Agent grant Read codes: the phone sets it for an agent while the grant is on; gates codes.query (codes the Macs found, brokered by the phone)
Phone and Mac: both set it for each other when they support the agents mirror; gates agents.state, agents.grant_set, codes.found and codes.read
Agent grant Detect codes (docs/mesh-and-codes.md): an agent sets it while it can run the code model; the phone sets it for an agent while the grant is on. Gates codes.candidate and codes.detected
Read-only active phone notification snapshots, only for an independently granted agent; ordinary notification broadcasts remain blocked

shape.notes: Sent by the side that dials. targetDeviceId (edition extension) names the trusted peer a reconnect is for; any other receiver closes quietly. Protocol 2: a first pairing sends commitment instead of publicKey, and reveals the key in pairing.reveal after the answer.
Protocol 2 first pairing: the initiator's ephemeral key after the answer. The responder checks it against the offer's commitment and fails the pairing on a mismatch.
proof is an HMAC under the pairing key; signature is P-256 over the session transcript.
Ends only the session it arrives on. reason (edition extension) says why, for the other screen. Tagged when the sender has an envelope key; after authentication only a tagged cancel is taken.
messageId echoes the ping's. Connection health (both apps) times the round trip from it; health puts nothing new on the wire and has no feature key.

payload.features: object of feature key to boolean; see features

shape.notes: Sent after pairing and whenever local policy changes. A feature is available only when both peers report true.

payload.(raw): UTF-8 text, not JSON, 1 to 32,768 bytes

shape.notes: text plus html at most 32 KiB.
messageId is the acknowledged message's ID.
Clipboard is off locally; followed by features.update.

payload.items: array of 1 to 100 {index, kind: text|html|image|file, mime (1 to 255 chars), name? (files, 1 to 255 chars), size (0 to 10 GiB), sha256? (base64 of 32 bytes), inline? (base64, all inline items at most 16 KiB decoded)}

payload.transferId: string, UUID chosen by the receiver

payload.code: expired | changed | too_large | unavailable | disabled | busy

payload.name: string, display name, last path component only
payload.purpose: edition extension: "clipboard" with offerId and index
payload.cameraRequestId: edition extension (camera_draft1): string, UUID of the Mac's open camera.request that this photo answers; older Macs ignore it and simply receive a file

shape.notes: Files is off locally; sent without decrypting the offer, followed by features.update.

payload.(raw): file bytes, at most 24 KiB per chunk, sequence from 0 without gaps

shape.notes: Between peers that both advertise files_fast_draft1 every chunk is a binary frame of kind 1 instead (transport.binaryFrames): up to 1 MiB, no envelope, the transfer ID and sequence bound into the AES-GCM tag.

Cumulative. The Mac keeps at most 64 chunks unacknowledged. With files_fast_draft1 the receiver acknowledges every binary chunk in every direction, and the sender keeps its unacknowledged bytes within a window that shrinks when the acknowledgements' round trip grows 40 ms over its minimum.

payload.sha256: string, base64 SHA-256 of all bytes

shape.notes: Idempotent.

payload.title: string, at most 1,024
payload.applicationIcon: string, optional base64 PNG, at most 28 KiB encoded
payload.actions: array of at most 4 {actionToken (at most 64), title (at most 64), allowsReply}
payload.redacted: boolean, edition extension, only with smsDefaultApp true or (email_codes_draft1) emailApp true
payload.emailApp: boolean, edition extension (email_codes_draft1), only to a Mac that shows the key: the notification came from a supported mail app (Gmail, Outlook, Proton Mail, Spark) and is not a group summary
payload.preview: string, optional, edition extension (email_codes_draft1), only with emailApp true: the expanded text (subject and body start), at most 600 UTF-16 units, cut only at whitespace; sent only when it looks like it holds a code. Never logged
payload.smsReply: boolean, edition extension (sms_draft1), only to a Mac that shows the key: the phone answers this notification by sms.send with notificationId
payload.smsThreadId: integer, optional, edition extension (sms_draft1): the conversation the message belongs to, when the phone found it

shape.notes: Content is sensitive and never logged. Smart routing chooses one alert recipient on the phone; compatible other Macs receive quiet history. Legacy peers receive content only if chosen, since they cannot honor quiet. Alert ownership sticks per logical message; a new message event may choose the current Mac. Calls and non-message updates stay pinned until removal; call/media state uses its independent all-device protocol.
Android runs only tokens it retained for the still active notification.

payload.reason: when not ok: bluetooth_off | unauthorized | unsupported | failed

payload.action: string (links: offer, or open to a Mac that advertises links_open_draft1; media: toggle | pause | next | previous | seek | volume)
payload.value: string (links: http(s) URL, at most 4,096 bytes; seek 0 to 604800; volume 0 to 100)
payload.sequence: integer, 1 to 2^53-1, per feature high-water mark

shape.notes: Edition extension (links_open_draft1): Send to device sends links action open. The Mac opens the link at once only when its own Open links from other devices right away setting is on (on when unset, explicit off preserved), at most one explicit link per phone every 3 seconds; otherwise it replaces the parked link in the menu bar.

payload.opened: edition extension (links_open_draft1): boolean, true when the Mac opened the link right away; older phones ignore it
payload.reason: optional string: rate_limited | browser_failed | links_disabled; explains a declined link

payload.player: string, the player's name, at most 64 chars
payload.title: string, at most 256 chars
payload.controls: optional array of toggle | pause | next | previous | seek | volume (absent: all)
payload.artwork: string, optional base64 JPEG, at most 16 KiB, at most 128x128

shape.notes: messageId is the request's ID. Senders time out after five seconds.

payload.number: string, 3 to 15 digits with optional leading +; spaces, parentheses, dots and hyphens are removed

shape.notes: At most one request every three seconds.
A phone that receives it answers input.session.stop, reason unsupported.

payload.reason: user | left_screen | screen_off | local_stop | timeout | disabled | permission_required | busy | invalid | unsupported

payload.text: string, 1 to 256 scalars, at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes, no Cc characters; never logged

payload.key: left | right | up | down | return | escape | tab | space | backspace | page_up | page_down | home | end | f5 | previous_app

payload.action: next | previous | start | end | black | laser_on | laser_move | laser_off
payload.x: integer 0 to 10,000 with laser_on and laser_move
payload.y: integer 0 to 10,000 with laser_on and laser_move

payload.actions: array of at most 64 {id, title, blocked?}. id: lock | sleep | screensaver | volume_up | volume_down | volume_mute | volume_set | app:<bundle id, [A-Za-z0-9.-], 1 to 155> | shortcut:<lowercase UUID>. title: 1 to 64 characters, no control characters, required for app: and shortcut: (phones show their own titles for the fixed ids). blocked: only permission_required (Lock without Accessibility)
payload.volume: optional {level: integer 0 to 100, muted: boolean}, while volume is allowed and the output has a settable volume

shape.notes: What this phone may run now; it replaces the previous list. Sent after each features.update that shows the key on both sides, and whenever the list, a switch, the grant or a permission changes. The phone drops single entries with an unknown id, a missing or bad title or a repeated id, and the whole catalog for a wrong version or more than 64 entries.

payload.action: string, an id from the latest catalog
payload.sequence: integer, 1 to 2^53-1, per session high-water mark, checked after the messageId window

shape.notes: Only an identifier from the Mac's own list goes on the wire: no command, argument, Shortcut name or text. A run that fails the version, requestId or sequence check is dropped; anything else gets exactly one actions.result. Rate limits per phone: volume 10 at once then 5 a second, other actions 3 at once then one every 2 seconds. The phone waits 10 seconds for the result (70 for a Shortcut), then reports it not confirmed.

payload.reason: with refused: not_allowed | invalid | rate_limited | busy | permission_required | unavailable | failed; phones read anything else as failed
payload.volume: optional {level, muted}: the volume after a volume action

shape.notes: The Mac keeps a private audit log of every run and refusal (owner-only, 30 days, at most 500 entries, never the value).

payload.active: boolean: the phone's Do Not Disturb (any interruption filter but all), or the Mac's Focus

shape.notes: Sent only while the sender's share switch is on and the peer's latest map shows the key: once after each features.update that shows it on both sides, then on every change. Applied only while the receiver's follow switch is on; a follower does not report the change it just made for 10 seconds, so two followers cannot loop.
One open request per Mac, at most one every 3 seconds; it expires after 2 minutes. The phone opens the camera only when unlocked and after a tap. A malformed request is dropped without an answer.

payload.status: opened | locked | permission_required | cancelled | busy | disabled | sending | failed; the Mac drops an unknown status

shape.notes: The photo itself arrives as a files.offer carrying cameraRequestId.

payload.edition: string, 1 to 32 UTF-8 bytes, rr for this edition
payload.app: string, installed version name, 1 to 64 UTF-8 bytes
payload.state: current | checking | available | downloading | ready | installing | needs_user | failed | manual
payload.target: string, optional, the version on offer, 1 to 64 UTF-8 bytes (available, downloading, ready, installing, needs_user; failed when known)
payload.reason: optional: with needs_user confirm | permission; with failed check | download | safety | installer | cancelled | not_applied | other; unknown reads as other
payload.remoteStart: boolean: Let paired devices start updates on this device is on and the updater can run
payload.checkedAt: integer, Unix ms of the last successful check, 0 for never
payload.auto: boolean, optional, default false: Update all devices automatically is on there and its updater can run
payload.busy: string, optional: what the person is doing there, so automatic updates wait: call | screen_share | remote_control | transfer | phone_files | setup; unknown reads as other (still busy)

shape.notes: Sent once after each features.update that shows the key on both sides, then on every change of a field other than progress, and while downloading at most once a second. A receiver drops a status with an unknown state, platform or channel, an auto that is not a boolean or a busy that is not a string. auto is written only when true, busy only when set.

payload.retry: boolean, optional, default false: the person tapped Retry for this device
payload.auto: boolean, optional, default false: started automatically (nobody tapped Update all); the receiver names the device that started it

shape.notes: Update yourself now from your own channel. It names no version, URL, file or channel: the receiver checks its own feed and installs only a newer build through its own checks (Android SHA-256 and signer, Mac Sparkle EdDSA), so it can never downgrade. Accepted only from a paired device whose map shows the key, while the receiver's Let paired devices start updates switch is on; at most one start every 30 seconds and five an hour per device. A start with a wrong version or a requestId that is not a UUID is dropped; anything else gets exactly one updates.result. Without retry, a device whose last attempt did not apply refuses not_applied. With auto, a device whose person is busy (a call, a screen share, remote control, a transfer, a Phone files download, setup or pairing) refuses busy.

payload.reason: with refused: disabled | rate_limited | manual | not_applied | busy (its updater cannot start now, or an automatic start found its person busy); senders read anything else as other

shape.notes: accepted also when an update was already running. Progress follows as updates.status.

payload.sims: array of at most 4 {subId (integer), slot (0 to 3), label (at most 64)}; empty when the phone cannot list them; an invalid entry is dropped
payload.cursor: {sms, mms}: integers, the newest _id in each SMS provider table

shape.notes: Sent after each features.update that shows the key on both sides, and when a permission or the SIM list changes.

payload.cursor: {sms, mms}: integers, the newest _id in each SMS provider table

shape.notes: The SMS provider changed (a ContentObserver, only while a Mac shows the key), at most one every 2 seconds. The Mac asks sms.sync when the cursor is ahead of its own and refreshes an open conversation.

payload.before: integer, optional, Unix ms, exclusive (absent: the newest)

payload.threads: array, newest first, of {threadId, participants (1 to 10 {address (at most 64), name (optional, at most 128)}), snippet (at most 160), date (Unix ms), unread (integer), subId (optional)}
payload.error: optional: disabled | permission (threads is then empty)

shape.notes: The phone stops adding entries before the plaintext limit and sets more.

payload.before: optional {date (Unix ms), id}, exclusive, ordered by date then id (absent: the newest)

payload.messages: array, newest first, of {id (s<n> or m<n>, at most 24), threadId, direction: in | out, status: received | pending | sent | delivered | failed (an unknown status reads as received or sent), date (Unix ms), address (at most 64; the other side, empty for an outgoing MMS), body (at most 4,000 UTF-16 units), truncated (optional boolean), subId (optional integer), read (optional boolean, default true), parts (optional, at most 8 images {partId (p<n>), mimeType image/*, size?})}; an invalid message is dropped

payload.since: {sms, mms}: integers, the newest _id in each SMS provider table, from the Mac's cache

payload.messages: array of messages newer than since (any order; the Mac sorts), as in sms.messages_page
payload.cursor: {sms, mms}: integers, the newest _id in each SMS provider table: where the next sms.sync starts
payload.reset: boolean: since is ahead of the phone or over 1,000 messages behind; the Mac drops its cache and loads the threads again

shape.notes: Each table is read in _id order, so the cursor never skips a message.

payload.body: string, 1 to 2,000 UTF-16 units, not only spaces
payload.threadId: integer, one of threadId, address and notificationId
payload.address: string, a phone number: + and 2 to 20 digits once spaces, dashes, dots and brackets are removed
payload.notificationId: string, at most 512: answers an SMS notification that carried smsReply
payload.subId: integer, optional: the SIM to send from (default: the thread's last SIM, else the phone's default)

shape.notes: One recipient only: a conversation with several people is refused (group). Emergency numbers are refused (invalid). At most one per second and 30 in 10 minutes per Mac. Bridgey never becomes the default SMS app; Android writes the sent message to the SMS provider. A reply to a notification goes through the messaging app's own reply when it has one, unless the phone's Send replies as SMS is on.

payload.status: sending | sent | delivered | failed | refused; the Mac drops an unknown status
payload.reason: with failed or refused: disabled | permission | invalid | group | no_sim | rate_limited | not_found | radio_off | no_service | failed (an unknown or missing reason reads as failed)
payload.via: optional: sms (SmsManager) | app (the messaging app's reply)

shape.notes: Several per request: sending, then sent or failed, then delivered when the network reports it.
Read-only MMS images. At most 4 open requests per Mac.

payload.data: string, base64 JPEG of at most 28,672 bytes, scaled down on the phone
payload.error: optional: not_found | unsupported | permission (no image fields)

shape.notes: The Mac keeps images in memory only.

payload.contacts: array of at most 20 {name (at most 128), address (at most 64), label (optional, at most 32)}

payload.threadIds: array of 1 to 50 integers, each at least 1 (repeats count once)

shape.notes: Read on the Mac: the phone runs the messaging app's own Mark as read (Notification.Action SEMANTIC_ACTION_MARK_AS_READ) on each notification it still shows for those conversations. Bridgey never writes to the SMS provider; a conversation without a notification stays unread on the phone.

payload.results: array of at most 50 {threadId (integer), result: marked | not_shown | no_action | failed (an unknown result reads as failed)}; an invalid entry is dropped

payload.address: string, optional, the number to block as in sms.send (shown to the person, never written by Bridgey)

shape.notes: Opens Android's own Blocked numbers screen (TelecomManager.createManageBlockedNumbersIntent): at once when Bridgey is in front, otherwise through a Bridgey notification the person taps. Only the default dialer or SMS app may write the blocked list, so the person adds the number there.

payload.result: opened | notified | unavailable (an unknown result reads as unavailable)

payload.rotate: optional boolean (Reset away-from-home identity); missing means false

shape.notes: Creates the pair secret: each side sends its contribution once per exchange (a side that receives one first answers with its own), then pairSecret = HKDF-SHA256(cLow || cHigh, salt bridgey-pair-secret-v1, info idLow 0x00 idHigh, 32). Started by the lower device ID when its pair check differs from the peer's connect.addresses. A malformed payload is dropped and the session stays.
Informational: the sender holds the new pair secret.

payload.port: integer 1 to 65535, the sender's UDP port
payload.addrs: array of at most 16 {a: IP address string, kind: lan | vpn | public6, vpn?: tailscale | other}; entries with an unknown kind or an unusable address are skipped
payload.pairCheck: optional string, base64url of HMAC-SHA256(pairSecret, bridgey-pair-check-v1)[0..8]; absent without a pair secret

shape.notes: Sent after every features.update that shows the key on both sides and whenever the sender's addresses change. The receiver keeps at most 16 per peer (30 days) and dials them over QUIC when the peer is away. The pair check never reveals the secret.

payload.seconds: integer, 2 to 15, how long each side sends
payload.link: object: platform (string, 1 to 16 bytes), network (wifi | ethernet | hotspot | other), optional band (2.4 | 5 | 6), linkMbps (1 to 100000), standard (4 to 7), widthMhz (20 to 320), lockHeld and screenOn (booleans, phones)

shape.notes: Speed test from the side that runs it. One test at a time per device; the other side answers within 5 seconds. Then ten speed.ping, then this side sends speed.data for `seconds`, then speed.turn, then the other side sends for `seconds` and answers speed.done.

payload.link: object, as in speed.start, with ready

shape.notes: transferId is the test ID, sequence 1 to 10. Answered at once with speed.pong carrying the same fields; the round trip shown is their median.
Acknowledges the speed.data binary frame with that test ID and sequence (cumulative). The sender paces on these exactly as on files.chunk.ack.

payload.bytesPerSecond: integer, 0 to 10^12, what the side that started measured from its acknowledgements after the first second

shape.notes: The side that started has finished sending: the other side sends now.

payload.bytesPerSecond: integer, 0 to 10^12, what this side measured

payload.forwardBytesPerSecond: optional integer, from the side that started to the other
payload.roundTripMs: optional number, 0 to 60000, median idle round trip
payload.loadedRoundTripMs: optional number, 0 to 60000, round trip of the acknowledgements while sending

shape.notes: So both apps can show the whole result.
Either side stops the test (transferId is the test ID): Stop, a stall of 5 seconds, or a failure.

payload.purpose: optional "browse" (files_browse_draft1): every place whatever the destination mode, plus writable, media and documents in the answer

payload.places: array of at most 17 {placeId, label (64), available, freeBytes}
payload.defaultFreeBytes: integer or null, free bytes where a send would land by default (every answer)
payload.writable: boolean, purpose browse only: "Allow other devices to change files here"
payload.media: purpose browse only: full | partial | none (photo and video access)
payload.documents: boolean, purpose browse only: at least one place is indexed for recent documents

payload.folders: array of folder names, at most 500 per page

payload.code: error code, see docs/protocol.md (browse adds read_only)

shape.notes: Also the failure answer to every browse request (places.files, media.*, places.download). Browse requests from a Mac whose files_browse_draft1 the phone did not advertise answer unsupported; over a lane budget, busy.

payload.placeId: string, default or a granted place
payload.cursor: string or null, opaque, from the previous page

shape.notes: Browse lane: 4 in flight and 40 per 10 s, else busy; answered within 8 s. Served in every folder destination mode. Errors not_found, place_unavailable, policy.

payload.entries: array of at most 200 {name (one existing component, 1 to 255 bytes), dir (boolean), size (integer, null for folders), modified (Unix ms or null), mimeType (null for folders), thumb (boolean)}

shape.notes: Folders first, then files, each in sort order (names case-insensitive, then exact). Hidden items and part files are neither listed nor counted.

payload.items: array of 1 to 100 refs ({placeId, path, name} or {mediaId}); a folder brings its subtree, hidden and system files skipped and counted

shape.notes: Browse lane. The phone then sends folders.offer with into: true and downloadRequestId; the Mac accepts a download offer only when it asked for it. Errors not_found, place_unavailable, limit_exceeded, busy, policy.

payload.folderTransferId: string, UUID of the folders.offer that follows

payload.kind: media (photos and videos, newest first) | files (recent documents in indexed places) | recent (both)

shape.notes: Browse lane.

payload.items: array of {ref, name, size, modified (Unix ms), mimeType, width, height, durationMs (null when unknown), thumb (boolean), location (display path, at most 128 characters), taken (Unix ms the gallery sorts by: date taken, else added; optional, for day headers)}
payload.access: full | partial | none (photo and video access; none returns no media items)
payload.indexing: boolean, the document index is refreshing

shape.notes: Askers cache by device ID, ref, modified and size: the same four always mean the same bytes.

payload.items: array of 1 to 64 {key (1 to 64 of [A-Za-z0-9_-], chosen by the asker), ref}
payload.replaces: string, optional, requestId of an earlier media request it cancels

shape.notes: Media lane: 4 active and 60 per 10 s, else busy. Answers are low priority: sent only while no file chunk, acknowledgement or control message waits.

payload.thumbs: array of {key, mimeType (image/webp from Android 11, else image/jpeg), width, height, tint (#rrggbb average colour), data (base64, at most 24 KiB decoded)}
payload.missing: array of keys without a thumbnail
payload.done: boolean, true on the last batch

shape.notes: In the order they are ready (made in the order asked, visible items first); askers match thumbnails by key. As many as fit in each batch. 45,056 bytes of plaintext keep the frame under the 65,536-byte limit after AES-GCM and base64.
Media lane. Videos answer with the poster frame. Errors not_found, unsupported.

payload.data: string, base64, at most 32 KiB decoded per part

shape.notes: Consecutive parts; the whole preview is at most 1 MiB.

payload.ref: ref to a file, not a folder

shape.notes: Media lane. Ranges are previews (hover prefetch, streamed playback) and carry no hash; a saved copy always goes through places.download.

payload.modified: integer, Unix ms, the whole file
payload.data: string, base64, at most 32 KiB decoded
payload.last: boolean, end of the range or of the file

payload.requestId: string, the media request to cancel

shape.notes: Not answered. Parts already on the wire may still arrive and are dropped by the asker.

payload.into: boolean, optional, default false (files_browse_draft1): entries land directly in the destination, top-level clashes saved as copies, nothing merged, replaced or asked
payload.downloadRequestId: string, UUID, optional (files_browse_draft1): the offer answers that places.download of the receiver

shape.notes: The Mac checks folders_draft1 before sending to a phone, the phone folders_receive_draft1 before sending to a Mac (no destination: a Mac serves no places). Uploads are into with destination; a phone rejects them read_only while it does not allow changes, policy while browsing is off.

payload.entries: array of at most 256 {type: dir | file, path, size?, sha256?, modified?}

payload.choices: array of merge | replace | new_folder | cancel

payload.completedBitmap: string, base64, bit i set when entry i is done
payload.freeBytes: integer or null, free bytes at the chosen destination (files_browse_draft1)

shape.notes: With Files off the receiver sends it outer only, without decrypting the offer.

payload.records: object of key to {value, changedAt, version, changedBy}, at most 32; every schema 1 key the sender syncs
payload.waiting: optional array of at most 32 keys that are on but wait for a permission on the sender
payload.first: optional bool: the sender has no first-connect answer for the receiver
payload.new: optional bool: the sender has no answer for any device

shape.notes: Sent by each side when settings_sync_draft1 becomes true on both for the session, including right after connecting. A snapshot never overwrites a chosen value: a setting the receiver never chose (version 0) takes the sender's chosen record; two different chosen values stay and show as Different on <device> with Apply to all. Schema 1 has 24 keys (docs/folders-and-settings-sync.md 8.4); unknown and per-device keys and invalid records are skipped one by one. A payload that fails decryption closes the session; one that fails validation is answered settings.error invalid_message.

payload.records: object of key to record, at most 32
payload.waiting: optional array of at most 32 keys
payload.answered: optional bool: the asker's person answered the first-connect question

shape.notes: Local edits and Apply to all (debounced 500 ms), relayed records from other peers, records that won (kept) and were not yet sent to this peer, and waiting list changes (records may be empty). A record that wins by the merge rule is applied.
kept lists keys where the receiver's own record won; it sends those records in settings.update unless it already sent them to this peer.
rate_limited: more than 20 settings.* messages from this peer in 10 seconds; the extra messages were dropped. Sent at most once per window.
Once per session after features.update; the phone shows app and os on the device page.

payload.grants: array of {key, state (on | off | waiting), window? (1h | today | 7d | forever), grantedAt?, expiresAt?, scope?}; keys files, clipboard, clipboard_request, notify, ask, ring, battery, codes, notifications

shape.notes: Sent after features.update and on every change, including a window that ended. Read-only on the agent.
The phone posts a notification that opens the device's permissions and marks the grants waiting for 24 hours or until Rahul decides. 3 an hour.

payload.status: ok | not_granted | rate_limited | invalid | busy | unknown | unsupported

shape.notes: Answers agent.grant_request, and refuses any agent request (notify.post, ask.request, clipboard.update, clipboard.rich, clipboard.request, find.start, ping.request, files.offer, codes.query).

payload.title: string, 1 to 120 characters
payload.tag: optional string, at most 64: replaces this device's earlier notification with that tag
payload.from: optional string, at most 64, shown as says it is from

shape.notes: Posted as plain text in the Agent messages channel. 30 an hour, burst 5; high priority 10 an hour.

payload.askId: string, UUID (UUIDv7 from the agent; a retry never posts twice)
payload.title: string, 1 to 120 characters
payload.options: array of 0 to 3 {id ([a-z0-9_-]{1,32}), label (1 to 20 characters)}; at most 2 with allowText; at least one option or allowText
payload.expiresAt: integer, Unix ms, at most 24 hours ahead

shape.notes: A high-importance notification in Agent questions. 20 an hour, 3 pending per agent, 10 on the phone.
Kept for 24 hours and sent again at the start of each session until the ask ends.

payload.expiresAt: integer, Unix ms, at most 10 minutes ahead

shape.notes: The phone asks with Send and Deny; Send opens Bridgey for a moment, because Android reads the clipboard only in the foreground. 10 an hour, 1 pending.

payload.html: optional string, with sent; text and html together at most 32 KiB

shape.notes: One bounded active snapshot, never a subscription, reply or dismiss action. Phone grant and authenticated session checked at delivery. No notification content in audit records.

payload.notifications: array of at most the requested limit: {id (128), packageName (256), applicationName (128), title (512), text (2048), postedAt (Unix ms)}; unavailable always empty
payload.truncated: boolean; more eligible items or the size budget was reached

payload.service: optional string, at most 64, matched case-insensitively

shape.notes: Each answered query is one codes.read audit entry on the phone and on the Mac. At most 2 held queries per agent.

payload.codes: array of at most 20 {code, service, source (sms | email), app, postedAt, latest, replaced, via}, newest first
payload.readers: integer, devices reading codes for this phone right now: Macs, and agents with Detect codes on

payload.source: sms (email is designed, not sent in phase 1)
payload.sender: string, at most 64 (the notification title, else the app's name)
payload.text: string, 1 to 600 UTF-16 units: the message with digit boxes joined, which passed the gate

shape.notes: Sent to one connected agent with Detect codes on, only while an agent has Read codes on and no Mac reads codes for this phone. One codes.detect audit entry on the phone and one on the agent; the text is never logged or stored.

payload.code: string, 4 to 12 letters or digits, with found only
payload.reason: optional string, at most 32, with failed only

shape.notes: Taken once per candidate, from the device it was sent to, within 30 seconds. The phone runs the guard on the code against the candidate text and sets the service itself, then keeps it like a Mac's codes.found.

payload.serviceKey: string, 1 to 64 (the sender, lowercased, when the Mac knows no service)

shape.notes: Only while the phone's latest agents.state lists an agent with Codes on. The phone keeps codes in memory for 15 minutes (at most 50), folded by serviceKey and code.
Never the code.

payload.agents: array of {deviceId, name, platform, app, os, pairedAt, lastSeenAt?, online, route?, grants (as in agent.grants), activity (newest 50 audit entries {at, action, outcome, detail?})}

shape.notes: After features.update with the key on both sides and on every change, at most once a second.
Applied as if switched on the phone, recorded as changed on that Mac.
